title: Beef, Steak and Kidney Pie
subtitle: slow-braised beef in shortcrust pastry
excerpt: Steak and kidney pie is a British pub classic of long-braised beef shin in a rich red wine gravy, enclosed in a buttery shortcrust pastry case. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Steak and kidney pie has been a cornerstone of British cooking since the Victorian era. It is one of the defining dishes of the British pub and working-class table.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the cooked filling without pastry. Defrost overnight, add fresh pastry and bake.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The filling is better made the day before. Cool and refrigerate overnight, then top with pastry and bake.

glossaryTerms.definition: A crumbly pastry made by rubbing fat into flour, used to line and top pies.
Slow-cooking meat in a small amount of liquid in a covered pan or oven.

Beef shin is the best cut for this pie because its high collagen content melts into the braising liquid, making the sauce silky without any thickening agent. Mushrooms add earthiness and bulk alongside the meat.
Toss the beef chunks in the plain flour to coat. Heat the butter in the dutch oven over high heat and brown the beef in batches. Set aside. Cook the onion in the same pot for 5 minutes.
Return the beef to the pot. Add the red wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes. Pour in the beef stock, add the mushrooms, bay leaves and thyme. Bring to a simmer.

Cover and cook over the lowest heat for 2 hours until the beef is completely tender. Remove the lid and simmer for 15 more minutes to thicken the sauce. Discard the bay leaves and thyme. Cool completely.

Make the shortcrust pastry: rub 125g cold butter into the strong flour until it resembles breadcrumbs. Add 4 to 5 tablespoons of cold water and bring together into a dough. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.

Spoon the cold filling into the baking tin. Roll out the pastry and drape it over the filling. Crimp the edges, cut a steam hole and brush with beaten egg. Bake at 200°C for 35 to 40 minutes until the pastry is golden. Rest for 10 minutes.

attrs.problem: The pastry is soggy on the underside.
attrs.solution: Make sure the filling is completely cold before adding the pastry lid. A hot filling steams the pastry from underneath.

attrs.problem: The beef is still tough after 2 hours.
attrs.solution: The heat was too high. Collagen in beef shin needs long, gentle heat to break down. Reduce to the barest simmer and give it another 30 minutes.

attrs.problem: The pastry shrinks away from the edges.
attrs.solution: Do not stretch the pastry as you lay it over the tin. Lay it gently and let it drape. Rested, cold pastry shrinks less than warm pastry.

content.text: Steak and kidney pie is a British pub staple, listed on chalkboard menus across England. It is serious winter food, served with mash and mushy peas. The dish appears in Victorian literature and has barely changed since. Home cooks make it for Sundays when there is time to tend the braise.
